newsitem.title: FRANCE: Volvo Cars on same retail-level as 1995.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Cars on same retail-level as 1995.

text.p: Volvo Cars is selling the same number of cars as last year, Volvo Cars' CEO Tuve Johannesson told Reuters in an interview on Monday.
"When it comes to retail we are roughly at the same level as this time last year," Johannesson said.

He declined to disclose Volvo's sales goal for 1996, or to comment on the figure of 382,000 cars sold this year, which he mentioned in June. In 1995, Volvo Cars sold 374,600 cars worldwide. One problem has been the production of Volvo's S40/V40 model at the NedCar plant in Born, Netherlands, which is still below planned output.

"We had problems at NedCar during March through May. Now those problems are over and the level of production there is above the originally planned level. We will meet the goal of producing 65,000 S40/V40 cars in 1996," Johannesson said.
Volvo never discloses forecasts of coming profits and Johannesson simply stated that he has "full control of the Volvo Cars company."
"The profit in the business is on the level I think it should be," Johannesson said.
